cells.tense: You are at the point where a shared meaning has deepened enough to carry you both further.
cells.ask: Say out loud what this connection asks of you now, and what you're willing to keep carrying so it stays alive.
cells.core:
You can tell what your shared history with certain people actually means, and you don't hold it politely at arm's length. You know which parts of it are still alive and which have gone quiet, and you carry that without making a production of it. When something you've built together reaches the point where it could go deeper or go flat, you don't flinch.

That steadiness isn't a mood you're in. It comes from having taken the whole of it in, including the parts you'd rather not name. What it can feed next is simple: an offer to the connection you're already in, said out loud, so the other side knows where you stand. That is the work here — not a bigger arrival, but a truer one, in your own voice.

cells.tense: You will be bracing for a departure that hasn't happened yet, and you're living there instead of here.
cells.ask: Bring one thing down to what it actually needs today, and do that smaller version before it's ready.
cells.core:
You're already living at the end. Every shared thing gets measured for whether it can survive what's coming, and you're rehearsing the leaving before anyone has left. That bracing looks like care, but it's putting your weight on a door that's still open, and the people on the other side can feel you halfway gone.

Something in the shared meaning has gone as far as it can, and part of you has caught on. The trouble isn't catching on. It's that you've jumped ahead of the living, so nothing gets built from where it actually is.

A small, real structure would give that energy somewhere to land. Make one thing with the people who are still here, at the scale it's actually at, and let it be what it is for now — not the version it'll have to become after you've gone.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you, still describing the room on the other side.
cells.ask: Write down one pattern in how you belong with people, plainly, and treat that page as the room you're actually standing in.
cells.core:
Something in how you belong with people has gone quiet, and you've stopped offering much of what you actually know about it. You can still say what the connection means, but saying it has turned into describing from a distance instead of standing inside it. The crossing came and went and you're still on the old side, telling it to yourself.

This isn't a shortage of depth. It's that the part of you that sees patterns has gone unused, so the pattern is running you instead of the other way around. Start where you actually are: take one thing you keep noticing about how this is going, put it into plain words, and let those words be a place you stand rather than a theory about where you used to stand. That's how the ground under you turns out to be the floor you're on.

cells.tense: You are at the point where this shared meaning turns, and you're calling it something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've called the situation and say out loud that you made it, then let it stand without defending it.
cells.core:
You're at the edge of what this connection can hold, and you've already started moving. It shows in what you bring up and what you quietly let drop, in which people you keep close and which you describe as having drifted. Yet it gets filed as something that came over the group, something that happened around you.

So the meaning you carry about what this bond is for ends up on somebody else's ledger, and what you've worked out doesn't reach the people it's about.

Name the thing you've been calling the way things are and claim it as yours, quietly, without making a case for it. The simpler layer of this is still there, and that's where you're actually standing.

attempts.check: The record supports that Passage turns on shared meaning reaching a threshold, and that the seat is becoming what you are; it does not support any claim that a person has a particular community, a particular departure, or a history of leaving or being left. The reader could reasonably say 'my leaving wasn't this, I didn't lose anything, my bond is fine' and still need what the card describes. The ask survives being wrong because it asks for spoken authorship of a tie or a turn, not for an act of exit. The line that serves the writer more than the person would be any sentence that tells them what their departure meant or what it will cost, so I've kept every cell to what the card's mechanism can actually carry.
